title: Indian Film Festival of Melbourne 2026 Unveils Program With Aamir Khan and Kantara in the Spotlight
excerpt: The 17th edition of IFFM runs August 13–23 with Aamir Khan headlining Independence Day celebrations and Rishab Shetty's Kantara sequel leading a stacked nomination list.
body:
• The 17th Indian Film Festival of Melbourne runs August 13–23, 2026, featuring screenings, awards, masterclasses and cultural events backed by the Victorian Government.
  • Aamir Khan headlines the festival with an Independence Day flag-raising ceremony, a film retrospective and an In Conversation session at Federation Square.
  • Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1, Sitaare Zameen Par and Lokah Chapter 1: Chandra lead a Best Film category spanning eight languages and genres.
  • The Best Actor race features Aamir Khan, Mammootty, Rishab Shetty, Ranveer Singh and Dulquer Salmaan among nominees from across Indian cinema.
https://youtube.com/watch?v=TMQUFhWm8C0

India's Biggest Film Festival Outside India Returns

The Indian Film Festival of Melbourne has unveiled its full programme for its 17th edition, running August 13 to 23. The festival — the largest celebration of Indian cinema outside of India — will feature premieres, special screenings, masterclasses, panel discussions and cultural events, all supported by the Victorian Government.

This year's edition places Aamir Khan at its centre. The actor will lead an Indian Independence Day flag-raising ceremony at Federation Square on August 16, followed by an open-air retrospective of his most acclaimed films — from Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988) to Dangal (2016) — screened on the venue's Big Screen. An In Conversation session at Zinc will give audiences a chance to hear Khan discuss his career in an intimate setting.

"The Remitly IFFM Dance Competition on August 16 brings together dancers from across Australia in styles ranging from Bollywood and hip hop to classical and folk."

Nominations Span Eight Languages

The festival's awards nominations reflect the breadth of Indian cinema in 2026. The Best Film category features productions in Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi and Bengali: Haq, Jarann, Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1, Lokah Chapter 1: Chandra, Saiyaara, Sitaare Zameen Par, Sharthopor and The Great Shamsuddin Family.

Rishab Shetty's Kantara sequel has emerged as a frontrunner following its blockbuster theatrical run, and Shetty himself earned dual recognition — nominated for both Best Director and Best Performance (Male).

The male acting category reads like a who's who of Indian cinema: Aamir Khan, Mammootty, Dulquer Salmaan, Ranveer Singh, Rishab Shetty, Ahaan Panday, Sanjay Mishra and Bhuman Bhargav Das. The Best Performance (Female) nominees include Yami Gautam Dhar, Rani Mukerji, Neena Gupta, Kirti Kulhari and Rajshri Deshpande.

"IFFM has grown into the most significant platform for Indian cinema outside of India, celebrating the art, the artists and the cultural connections that film creates across borders."

— IFFM organisers

Beyond the Big Screen

The festival extends well beyond film screenings. The Remitly IFFM Dance Competition on August 16 brings together dancers from across Australia in styles ranging from Bollywood and hip hop to classical and folk. Celebrity judges Malaika Arora and casting director Mukesh Chhambra will select winners from the competition stage at Federation Square.

Best Indie Film nominees feature titles in Kannada, Punjabi, Tamil, Assamese and Hindi, including Ammang Haelbeda (Don't Tell Mother), Kikkran De Phull (Flowers of Acacia) and Not a Hero. The Best Series category features Kohrra: Season 2, Matka King, Freedom at Midnight: Season 2 and Real Kashmir Football Club, reflecting the growing importance of streaming content in Indian entertainment.

A Cultural Bridge for the Diaspora

For Australia's rapidly growing Indian community — now estimated at over one million — IFFM serves as both a cultural anchor and a bridge between communities. The festival provides a platform for Indian filmmakers to reach global audiences while giving diaspora audiences a connection to the storytelling traditions of home.

The Victorian Government's continued backing underscores the festival's economic and cultural significance to Melbourne, which has positioned itself as a hub for Asian cultural events in the Southern Hemisphere.

What to Watch

Winners across all categories will be decided by an independent jury of Australian film industry professionals and announced at the closing ceremony. Tickets and the full screening schedule are available through the festival's official website. For NRIs in Melbourne and across Australia, IFFM 2026 offers 10 days of cinema that captures the full spectrum of Indian filmmaking — from big-budget spectacles to independent voices that rarely get a theatrical window abroad.
